text: The exact volumes of 1 M NaOH solution required to neutralise 50 mL of $1 M H_{3}PO_{3}$ solution and 100 mL of $2 M H_{3}PO_{2}$ solution, respectively, are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Millimoles of $H_{3}PO_{3} = M$ $\times$ V = 1 $\times$ 50 = 50

For 1 millimole of $H_{3}PO_{3}$, we require 2 millimoles of NaOH.

For 50 millimole of $H_{3}PO_{3}$, we require (2 $\times$ 50) = 100 millimoles of NaOH.

Millimoles of NaOH = M $\times$ V = 100

1 $\times$ V = 100

V = 100 mL


[IMG]


Millimoles of $H_{3}PO_{2} = M$ $\times$ V = 2 $\times$ 100 = 200

For 1 millimole of $H_{3}PO_{2}$, we require 1 millimoles of NaOH.

For 200 millimoles of $H_{3}PO_{2}$, we require 200 millimoles of NaOH.

So, volume of NaOH = 200 mL

text:
Arrange the following metal complex/compounds in the increasing order of spin only magnetic moment. Presume all the three, high spin system.

(Atomic numbers Ce = 58, Gd = 64 and Eu = 63)

$(a) (NH_{4})_{2}$[$Ce(NO_{3})_{6}$]

$(b) Gd(NO_{3})_{3}$ and 

$(c) Eu(NO_{3})_{3}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) ${}_{58}Ce\to [Xe]4f^{2}5d^{0}6s^{2}$

In complex $Ce^{+4}\to [Xe]4f^{0}5d^{0}6s^{0}$

There is no unpaired electron, so, $μ_{m}$ = 0 BM

(B) ${}_{64}Gd\to [Xe]4f^{7}5d^{1}6s^{2}$

In complex, ${}_{64}Gd^{2+}\to [Xe]4f^{7}5d^{1}$

There are 8 unpaired electrons.

$\therefore$ $μ_{m}=\sqrt{8(8+2)}=\sqrt{80}=8.94BM$

(C) ${}_{63}Eu\to [Xe]4f^{7}5d^{0}6s^{2}$

In complex ${}_{63}Eu^{+3}\to [Xe]4f^{6}5d^{0}6s^{0}$

contain six unpaired electrons.

So, $μ_{m}=\sqrt{6(6+2)}=\sqrt{48}BM=6.93BM$

Hence, order of spin only magnetic moment

$B>C>A$.

text: A 5.0 m mol $dm^{-3}$ aqueous solution of KCl has a conductance of 0.55 mS when measured in a cell of cell constant $1.3 cm^{-1}$. The molar conductivity of this solution is $___________$ mSm$^{2}$ mol$^{-1}. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Conductance = $\frac{Conductivity}{Cellconstant}$

$\therefore$ Conductivity = 0.55 $\times$ $10^{-3}$ $\times$ $1.3 S cm^{-1}$

Molar conductivity = $\frac{Conductivity(Scm^{-1})\times 1000}{Molarity(mol/L)}$

$=\frac{0.55\times 10^{-3}\times 1.3\times 1000}{5\times 10^{-3}}$

$= 143 S cm^{2}$ mol$^{-1}$

$= 14.3 mS m^{2}$ mol$^{-1}$

$\approx$ $14 mS m^{2}$ mol$^{-1}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift

text:
At 25${}^{\circ }$C, 50 g of iron reacts with HCl to form FeCl$_{2}$. The evolved hydrogen gas expands against a constant pressure of 1 bar. The work done by the gas during this expansion is $_________ J. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer).

[Given : R = 8.314 J mol$^{-1} K^{-1}$. Assume, hydrogen is an ideal gas] [Atomic mass of Fe is 55.85 u]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Fe}\quad +2\mathrm{HCl}\longrightarrow \mathrm{FeCl}{}_{2}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$

One mole of Fe gives one mole of $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$:

$n_{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}}=n_{\mathrm{Fe}}=\dfrac{50}{55.85}=0.8953\text{mol}$

Only $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$ is a gas (HCl and $\mathrm{FeCl}{}_{2}$ are in aqueous solution), so the volume increase is the volume of hydrogen formed at $p_{\text{ext}}=1$ bar: $\Delta V=\dfrac{n_{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}}RT}{p_{\text{ext}}}$.

The work done by the gas against the constant external pressure is

$w_{\text{by gas}}=p_{\text{ext}}\Delta V=n_{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}}RT=0.8953\times 8.314\times 298=2218\text{J}$

In the chemistry sign convention, the corresponding work done on the system is $w=-2218$ J.

Hence, the answer is 2218.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift

text: A and B decompose via first order kinetics with half-lives 54.0 min and 18.0 min respectively. Starting from an equimolar non reactive mixture of A and B, the time taken for the concentration of A to become 16 times that of B is $_________ \min . ($Round off to the Nearest Integer).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Initially : $[A_{0}]=[B_{0}]=a$

After time 't' min : $[A]=16[B]$

$[A]=[A_{0}]e^{-k_{A}t}$

$[B]=[B_{0}]e^{-k_{B}t}$

$\Rightarrow a.e^{-k_{A}t}=16ae^{-k_{B}t}$

$\Rightarrow e^{-(k_{A}-k_{B})t}=16$

$\Rightarrow (k_{B}-k_{A})t=\ln 16$

$\Rightarrow \ln 2\left (\frac{1}{18}-\frac{1}{54}\right )t=4\ln 2$

$\Rightarrow t=\frac{54\times 18\times 4}{36}=108$ min
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift

text: In Duma's method of estimation of nitrogen, 0.1840 g of an organic compound gave 30 mL of nitrogen collected at 287 K and 758 mm of Hg pressure. The percentage composition of nitrogen in the compound is $__________. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer). [Given : Aqueous tension at 287 K = 14 mm of Hg]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Aqueous tension at 287 K = 14 mm of Hg.

Hence actual pressure = (758 – 14)

= 744 mm of Hg.

Moles of $N_{2}=\frac{(758-14)}{760}\times \frac{30\times 10^{-3}}{0.0821\times 287}$

$=1.246\times 10^{-3}$ mol

mass of $N_{2}=1.246\times 10^{-3}\times 28$

mass % of $N_{2}$ $=\frac{massof{}^{'}N^{'}}{totalmass}\times 100$

$=\frac{1.246\times 28\times 10^{-3}}{0.184}\times 100$

$=\frac{124.6\times 28}{0.184}%=18.96%$

$\simeq 19%$

text: Sulphurous acid $(H_{2}SO_{3})$ has $Ka_{1} = 1.7$ $\times$ $10^{-2}$ and $Ka_{2} = 6.4$ $\times$ $10^{-8}$. The pH of $0.588 M H_{2}SO_{3}$ is $__________. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$Ka_{1}$ of $H_{2}SO_{3}>>Ka_{2}$ of $H_{2}SO_{3}$

$\therefore$ The contribution of $H^{+}$ from $2^{nd}$ dissociation of $H_{2}SO_{3}$ can be neglected.


[IMG]


$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{cα^{2}}{1-α}=1.7\times 10^{-2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{0.588α^{2}}{1-α}=1.7\times 10^{-2}$

$\Rightarrow 58.8α^{2}=1.7-1.7α$

$\Rightarrow 58.8α^{2}+1.7α-1.7=0$

$α=\frac{-1.7+\sqrt{1.7^{2}+4\times 1.7\times 58.8}}{2\times 58.8}=0.156$

$[H^{+}]=cα=0.092$

$pH=-\log [H^{+}]$

$=1.036$

$\approx 1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift
